title: Operating-System Compatibility knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Operating-System Compatibility”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “GNU versus BSD utility differences” under lesson 151, “Operating-System Compatibility”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Operating-System Compatibility”?
options: Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Check external command versions, validate input, set timeouts, and handle failures explicitly.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
questions.answer_key: Check external command versions, validate input, set timeouts, and handle failures explicitly.
questions.explanation: Check external command versions, validate input, set timeouts, and handle failures explicitly. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Operating-System Compatibility”?
options: Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Declare the target interpreter and test the feature set on the oldest supported environment.
questions.answer_key: Declare the target interpreter and test the feature set on the oldest supported environment.
questions.explanation: Declare the target interpreter and test the feature set on the oldest supported environment. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
